result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You were in hospital from 5 October 2026 to 7 October 2026. You had a chest infection (community-acquired pneumonia). It was in the lower part of your right lung.
Your CURB-65 score was 1. This is a score doctors use to judge how serious a chest infection is.
In hospital you had antibiotics into a vein (IV) for 1 day. Then you had amoxicillin tablets.
You may feel tired for several weeks. Your cough may last 3 to 6 weeks.

## What you need to do
1. Take your amoxicillin tablets for 3 more days. This makes 5 days of antibiotics in total.
2. Have a repeat chest X-ray in 6 weeks at the Radiology Department. This checks that the infection has cleared.
3. Do not book the X-ray. You do not need to book it. A request has been sent.

## Dates and medicines
- 5 October 2026: you went into hospital.
- 7 October 2026: you left hospital.
- 10 October 2026: your last dose of amoxicillin.
- In 6 weeks: repeat chest X-ray. No exact date is given.

Medicine:
- Amoxicillin, 500 milligrams, three times a day (TDS).
- You had 2 days of antibiotics in hospital. You take tablets for 3 more days.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- When will I get the date for my chest X-ray?
- How will I hear the result of my X-ray?
- How long may my tiredness and cough last?

## When to get urgent help
See your GP or call 111 if:
- you become more short of breath
- your fever comes back
- you cough up blood

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
